title: Moses's Family Challenges Him
overview: Moses's sister and brother question his special role as God's spokesman, and God defends him, striking Miriam with a skin disease that sends her outside the camp for seven days.

parts.label: Sister and brother complain (vv. 1-3)
parts.note: Miriam and Aaron, Moses's own sister and brother and leaders themselves, criticize his marriage to a woman from Cush, a land south of Egypt; it is unclear whether she is his wife Zipporah or a second wife. They go on to ask whether God speaks only through Moses, and a side remark on his humility explains his silence, though many think a later editor added it.

parts.label: Called to the tent (vv. 4-5)
parts.note: God suddenly summons all three to the tent of meeting, the sacred tent where God met with Moses, and appears in a pillar of cloud. Aaron and Miriam are called forward at the entrance, like people brought before a judge.

parts.label: Why Moses is different (vv. 6-8)
parts.note: Other prophets hear from God through dreams and visions, but God speaks with Moses directly and plainly and trusts him with the whole household of Israel, so speaking against him means speaking against God's choice. Christians later read this through the letter to the Hebrews, which calls Moses faithful as a servant in God's house and Jesus faithful as a son.

parts.label: Miriam is struck (vv. 9-12)
parts.note: When the cloud lifts, Miriam's skin is white with a disease (the Hebrew term covers various skin conditions, not only modern leprosy), and the text does not say why only she is struck. Many think it is because she led the complaint, and a frightened Aaron admits their wrong and begs that she not waste away like a stillborn child.

parts.label: Seven days outside (vv. 13-16)
parts.note: Moses cries out for her healing, yet she must spend seven days outside the camp, the same time of shame a daughter would bear if her father spat in her face. The text never says exactly when she recovers, but the whole people wait for her return before moving on.

disagreement: Christians differ on how much the complaint about Moses's Cushite wife was about her ethnicity, and so whether the chapter speaks against prejudice, or whether the marriage was only a pretext for a struggle over authority.
think: When someone close to you is given more recognition or authority than you, how do you tell honest criticism apart from envy?
